name: phase2_tier2_feasibility
description: Does the operand modulate FREQUENCY, not just power? Tiers 2 and 3 of the
receiver ladder read frequency (world-readable scaling_cur_freq) and
self-timing dilation, so both need a DVFS response to observe. Under
Config-A there is none by construction; this runs under Config-B.
A first pass (results/20260903-132837, interrupted after 6 runs) answered
the question yes and reshaped this spec three ways.
1. The response is large where it exists: 10 threads on the P-cores drew
46.9 W at 3694 MHz and swung 804 MHz between the two operands, which
scaling_cur_freq would read easily. Four threads gave only -195 MHz
with a CI that barely excluded zero.
2. The sign is negative and that is the physics, not an artifact: the
heavier operand draws more power, the part throttles, and the measured
frequency AND package power both fall. Under Config-B the power delta
inverts relative to Config-A for this reason, so watts are no longer
the quantity to read.
3. Adding the E-cores was counterproductive. 18 threads drew less power
than 10 (31 W vs 47 W) because memory bandwidth saturates and per-
thread throughput collapses. The ladder therefore stays on P-cores.
The first pass put its A/A at 18 threads, which was the wrong place: a
control belongs at the configuration whose effect is being claimed. The
A/A here is at 10 threads. Under Config-B its job is harder than usual --
turbo leaves large slow swings in both power and frequency, and the first
pass's A/A frequency deltas were -104 and -75 MHz with confidence
intervals comfortably containing zero. That is the noise this has to beat.
t4_s2 is the standard Phase 1 placement, kept so this session can be
compared with the Config-A work. The rest hold stride 1 and vary only the
thread count, so they form a dose axis rather than a change of kind.
Read the MHz column per condition, not the watts.
